requirement: All assessments MUST use the SDK graph and source tools. A read uses the node address under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.mcp`. A delivered read records that node’s fingerprint under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`. The source project follows {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`.
rationale:
structural: The only structural obligation in `requirements.authoring.source_tools` is the clause "All assessments MUST use the SDK graph and source tools". An alternative that gave the model its own file-reading tools, or ran assessments outside the SDK validation graph, would be a different implementation. The cited read and fingerprint clauses and the local provider scope are context. They are cited, not implemented here.

The roots support that obligation:
- `src/authoring/domain_tools.rs#fn[configure]` attaches the SDK `Sources` provider, rooted at the project directory, to the SDK validation cache with `with_sources(Sources::new(...))`. It then installs the agent configuration with `set_agent`. It adds only the Habeas-specific tools (`LookupRequirements`, `RunNamedQuery`, `Github`) on top of the SDK tools.
- `src/authoring/sdk.rs#fn[run]` builds the graph from `sources.domain`, calls `domain_tools::configure`, and drives each review through the SDK `Validator::verify`. It then takes the observed node dependencies from the verified result.
- `src/authoring/sdk.rs#impl[Review<'_>]/fn[ask]` issues the model request through the SDK `ValidationContext` (`cx.ask`). It adds `contents_of_current_node` and `contents_of_node` inputs, so delivered contents are recorded by the SDK.

These three roots cover the graph and source-tool delegation, so no gap remains.

behavioral: The obligations in `requirements.authoring.source_tools` are covered. The three cited requirements are context only. I did not reassess their own tests, which the SDK tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs` and `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs` cover.

1. **Assessments use the SDK graph and source tools.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools]` runs a full assessment. It asserts that the tool set sent to the model is exactly the graph and source tools: `read_node`, `outgoing_edges`, `lookup_requirements`, `run_named_query`, `list_sources`, `outline_source`, `search_text`, `search_structure`, `finish_search`, `get_next_page`, `github` and `submit_result`. It also asserts that the model's `read_node` call returns the source payload. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_and_example_assessments_record_selected_and_explicit_reads]` repeats this for citation and example assessments. It runs `search_text`, `finish_search` and `read_node` calls by path and selector, and by `Definition` node. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[explicit_ignored_reads_return_an_error_and_the_assessment_continues]` exercises `list_sources`, `search_text` and `search_structure` through the CLI.

2. **A read uses the node address (`read_node.mcp`).** The Bedrock test checks the `read_node` input schema, which has the `path`, `location`, `node` and `data` fields. It reads by path plus location. The citation test reads by path plus selector and by `data` Definition. The ignored-reads test covers a missing path (the error names `missing.rs`) and a malformed `node` (the error says "invalid node ID"). It also covers an excluded path, which returns an error that names the file and says it is excluded, without leaking the content.

3. **A delivered read records the node's fingerprint (`read_node.inputs`).** The Bedrock test compares the evidence `inputs` for `extra.txt` with `outline_inputs_for_lines`, so the fingerprint is recorded for the delivered read. The citation test checks that the inputs contain the outline inputs for `fn[first]` and `fn[second]`, which are the nodes the search and read touched. It also checks that the explicitly read definition is recorded with its text, and that `fn[untouched]` is not recorded. The ignored-reads test asserts that the denied read leaves no input in the evidence, so a failed read records no observation.

4. **The source project follows the local provider.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` runs with and without a Git repository. It covers these cases:
   - nested `.gitignore` exceptions;
   - a tracked file that is still ignored;
   - an exception inside an ignored directory;
   - listing, reading, parsing and text search, including requests that name a file or subdirectory directly;
   - `.git` metadata being excluded, and reads of it returning an error;
   - scopes outside the project, such as `..`, returning an error.
   `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_inputs_can_read_untracked_declarations_and_terms]` shows that untracked, non-ignored files are available. The CLI test shows the same ignore scope in the agent tools: an ignored file reads as an error, and listing and text and structural search return nothing for ignored content.

I found no uncovered obligation. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/search.rs#mod[tests]/fn[byte_search_reports_case_sensitive_one_based_matching_lines]` and `tests/live_bedrock.rs#fn[live_bedrock_authoring]` are additional supporting tests.

text: :::{req} source_tools

All assessments MUST use the SDK graph and source tools. A read uses the node address under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.mcp`. A delivered read records that node’s fingerprint under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`. The source project follows {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`.
:::{req} read_node.mcp
Give `read_node` a node address under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`. The result contains the node’s text. If more
text remains, pass `next` to `get_next_page`.
```text
read_node(NodeAddress) -> {text: string, next?: UUID}
// For a source node the result has these additional fields:
{file: string, selector: string, children: {node: NodeId, file: string, selector: string, header?: string}[]}
:::{req} read_node.inputs
A successful `ValidationContext::read` records the node's identity and the
fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
For a Rust caller, the SDK records the fingerprint when `read` returns the
contents. For an agent, the harness puts a tool result in the next request to
the model and records the fingerprint once the provider responds successfully.
That successful exchange is *delivery*. For example, suppose the tool reads a
function that returns `3`, and someone changes it to return `4` before the
provider responds. The model saw the version that returns `3`, so the SDK
records the fingerprint it computed from that version. Reading the function
again at this point would record a fingerprint for code the model never saw.
:::{req} local_provider
Source inspection uses the project directory and respects `.gitignore`,
including nested ignore files and their exceptions. Untracked files are
available unless ignored. The same scope applies to listing, reading,
outlining, text search, and structural search, including requests naming a
file or subdirectory directly.
Files outside the project directory and Git metadata are excluded. A direct
read of an excluded file returns an error.
